video_title: Michael Porter Jr. Explains What Went WRONG With Cam Thomas in Brooklyn

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. on Cam Thomas's struggles in Brooklyn
quotes.excerpt: It's a lot more to the NBA and sticking around than just that.
quotes.quote: I don't know really what the public narrative is about Cam. I know that when it comes to putting the ball in the hoop and making tough shots, I know he is one of the best. But there's a lot of things, as you know in the NBA, that it's a lot more to the NBA and sticking around than just that. I think for Cam, it was a mixture of he was frustrated with a lot of things and then also his personality. He was just a certain type of way, real quiet, stuck to himself, always had his headphones in, listening to YoungBoy every day, and all he wanted to do is hoop. He doesn't really socialize. He'll come to the gym sometimes and he'll say two words all day, all practice. He doesn't really talk to nobody.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Why Cam Thomas struggled to adapt to a larger role
quotes.excerpt: I don't know if he was willing to break out of his personality and be talkative.
quotes.quote: When it comes to a team willing to pay you and come off that money and you're a number one option and it comes with so much more, I don't know if he was willing to break out of his personality and be talkative and try to be a leader and try to bring guys together. I think that's kind of what happened here in Brooklyn. He was frustrated about the contract the year before and the fact that Brooklyn didn't really pay him how he wanted to. From his perspective, he's thinking talent-wise, he's as good as Austin Reaves, he's as good as Jalen Green, he's as good as this guy, that guy, and they're getting paid $100 million contracts.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: Kendrick Perkins on the importance of team communication
quotes.excerpt: You want to see your best players not hijack the offense.

text_blocks.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
text_blocks.text: He is a legit bucket getter. The narrative behind him is he does, you know, Richard said basketball is just more about playing one-on-one. At times, you want to see your best players not hijack the offense. A lot of guys on bad teams hijack an offense where everyone is just standing around. Some of the best scorers in the league do that at times, but if you can't pass, get the ball back, and then allow other people to touch the ball and you just go, that's not going to work because every game we're not just going to throw you the ball when you're playing with other players who are getting $80, $90, $100 million.

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: And then also, a crazy stat is basketball, this isn't football. You got to play defense too. And I think statistically he was the worst defender per minute in the game.

quotes.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
quotes.summary_phrase: The high stakes of the NBA and player development
quotes.excerpt: The NBA is a different game. It's the highest level, it's the best players.
quotes.quote: The NBA is a different game. It's the highest level, it's the best players, it's the most at risk, it's all of these things. And all of those things go into a pot in order for you to make it. So if you have a little deficiencies, whether it's your personality, whether it's your game, whether it's your whatever, all of those things can shift a player from being elite to just okay or from okay to out the league. Cam Thomas I think was an elite scorer. I was always taught, if you want to really be on the court, you got to be able to do two things well.
